skill.name: Database Manager
skill.description: Manage Supabase schemas, migrations, Row Level Security policies, queries, and troubleshooting guidance for the CookMode V2 database.

skill.author: AdamFehse

security_audit.summary: All 40 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline-code markers and fenced SQL or JavaScript examples, not shell execution or reconnaissance. The skill documents permissive Supabase Row Level Security policies that allow unrestricted database access and should not be used outside a trusted environment.

remediation.issue: The documented current and template RLS policies allow every client to read and modify protected tables.
remediation.suggestion: Replace FOR ALL USING (true) policies with authenticated, role-based policies that scope access to the appropriate tenant, user, or kitchen.

remediation.issue: The migration template normalizes an unrestricted RLS policy for new tables.
remediation.suggestion: Provide a secure-by-default policy template and require an explicit documented exception for trusted shared deployments.

remediation.issue: Examples include destructive database operations without operational safeguards.
remediation.suggestion: Require backups, review, and testing before applying schema changes or destructive queries in production.

semantic_findings.title: Unrestricted Row Level Security Policies
semantic_findings.description: The skill describes and templates policies using FOR ALL USING (true), allowing any client with database access to read and modify table data. This is unsafe for multi-tenant or untrusted deployments.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The policy statements explicitly grant all operations with a universally true condition, and the file acknowledges that user-specific policies are needed for multi-tenant setups.

content.value_statement: Database changes can be difficult to plan and review. This skill provides CookMode V2 schema context, migration patterns, query examples, and troubleshooting guidance.
actual_capabilities: Explains the five documented CookMode V2 tables and their fields.
Provides SQL patterns for creating and modifying tables and indexes.
Shows Supabase client examples for selecting, upserting, and deleting data.
Documents the current real-time table subscriptions and connection flow.
Provides troubleshooting steps for sync, constraint, and RLS issues.
limitations: It is specific to the documented CookMode V2 database design.
It does not apply migrations or access a live Supabase project.
Its permissive RLS examples are unsuitable for multi-tenant applications.
It does not replace database backups, testing, or human review.

use_cases.title: Add a database feature
use_cases.description: Plan a new CookMode table, indexes, migration steps, and real-time updates.

use_cases.title: Diagnose synchronization issues
use_cases.description: Review real-time subscriptions, RLS policies, and client connection checks.

use_cases.title: Review a schema change
use_cases.description: Check constraints, migration sequencing, rollback notes, and production safeguards.

prompt_templates.title: Understand a table
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the recipe_status table, its constraints, and how the application uses it.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a migration to add a nullable notes field to recipe_status. Include validation, indexes, rollback notes, and testing steps.

prompt_templates.title: Create secure RLS policies
prompt_templates.prompt: Replace the permissive RLS policy for recipe_notes with authenticated, tenant-scoped access policies. State all assumptions before writing SQL.

prompt_templates.title: Review a production change
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this proposed CookMode schema change for data loss, locking, RLS exposure, real-time effects, rollback, and deployment order: [describe change].

output_examples.input: Plan a migration for recipe notes.
output: Proposed a recipe_notes table with a recipe reference and timestamps.
Listed an index, secure RLS requirements, rollback steps, and local test checks.

output_examples.input: Why are ingredient updates not syncing?
output: Check the real-time subscription and browser console errors.
Verify the table is published and its RLS policy permits the intended operation.
The documented policy permits all reads and writes.
Replace it with authenticated, scoped rules before a multi-tenant deployment.

best_practices: Test every migration on representative data before production deployment.
Back up data and document rollback steps before destructive changes.
Use authenticated, scoped RLS policies instead of unrestricted access.
anti_patterns: Do not apply schema changes directly in production without review.
Do not use permissive RLS policies for untrusted or multi-tenant users.
Do not drop tables or columns before confirming backups and dependencies.

faq.question: Does this skill connect to Supabase?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples but does not access a live project.

faq.question: Can I use the RLS examples in production?
faq.answer: Only in a trusted shared environment. Use scoped authenticated policies for multi-tenant deployments.

faq.question: Does it create migration files?
faq.answer: It can help draft migration content and naming, but you must review and apply the file.

faq.question: Which tables does it document?
faq.answer: It documents ingredient checks, step checks, recipe status, order counts, and chef names.

faq.question: Can it help with real-time issues?
faq.answer: Yes. It identifies the documented subscriptions and suggests checks for policies and client errors.

faq.question: Should I back up before a migration?
faq.answer: Yes. Back up production data and test the migration before applying it.
